earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists exist (Shaw 1979, Z'graggen 1975, Franklin 1973 per Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions); no grammar or phonology of Fembe/Agala published.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel (1986). The Bosavi language family. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24, Pacific Linguistics A-70, pp. 45-76. DOI 10.15144/PL-A70.45
sources.note: Cursory comparative phonology only. Table 1 (p. 48) 'Phonemic inventories for Bosavi Family languages' gives Agala a supra-segmental column of 'N, LB, OS' (= nasalisation, labialisation, open syllable); p. 49: 'The supra-segmental phonemes of vowel nasalisation and length, and open versus closed syllables, all play a role in the phonemic inventory of the region.' Stress and tone are never mentioned for Agala or any other language; author warns 'the data are too limited to state precise phonological rules'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid femb1238 (Hammarström et al.), references list
sources.note: Bibliographic only: subclassification sources Shaw 1986 and Dwyer, Minnegal & Woodyard 1993; endangerment from Campbell et al. 2022. No grammar, phonology or sketch listed; alt names Agala, Sinale.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives OAI harvest (41,757 records, to 2024-04-14), local cache _sil_oai; SIL.org search page for agl (could not be reached by automated download); ELAR search 'Fembe' (0 results)
sources.note: No SIL record carries language code [agl]; no ELAR deposit. SIL has published nothing on Fembe (no survey report, no OPD, no phonology).

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström (2018). The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (Open chapter, OAPEN 20.500.12657/23719.)
sources.note: Nothing for Fembe/Agala. The East Strickland entry (2.3.1.10) is a classificatory listing: 'A long dialect chain from Konai in the north down to Odoodee in the south.. divided into six languages by Shaw (1986)'; 'Fembe [agl] 350; wordlist: Shaw 1986, Z'graggen 1975a'; one putative pTNG reflex 'Agala: fulu(ma) ali to fly > *pululu-'. The prosody survey (2.4.3, Donohue 1997 / Ross 2005b typology of syllable tone, word tone, pitch accent) discusses Paniai Lakes, Awyu-Dumut, Asmat-Kamoro, Goilalan, Binanderean, Koiarian, Baraic, Mek, Marindic, Kutubuan, Somahai, Enga-Kewa-Huli, Turama-Kikori, Kai…

sources.citation: Gérard, Anaïs (2017). Procuring game, procuring money: dilemmas of relationality with outsiders among Febi people, Western Province, Papua New Guinea. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne (open redacted version, hdl 11343/198374).
sources.note: No phonology content: an ethnographic thesis with scattered Febi lexemes (italicised, no diacritics), myths in English translation, a bird-name appendix; cites Shaw 1986 lexicostatistics (Febi shares 78% with Kubo, 67% with Konai) and Årsjö & Årsjö 2000 Konai survey. Nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Minnegal, Monica & Peter D. Dwyer (2017). Navigating the Future: An Ethnography of Change in Papua New Guinea. Canberra: ANU Press (Asia-Pacific Environment Monograph 11). Open access (OAPEN 20.500.12657/31270).
sources.note: Only an orthographic caveat (nasalisation unmarked; regional pronunciation differences); no phonology, nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Dwyer, Peter D. & Monica Minnegal (2016). Counting systems of the Strickland-Bosavi languages, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 34(1): 1-36. (hdl 11343/59568)
sources.note: No phonology. Gives the Febi body-part tally (28-cycle, recorded by A. Gérard at Gesesu 2009) and Table 16 'Some counting words used by Febi-speakers' from Dan Shaw's SIL wordlists (Burnett River headwaters 1971, Kuobi/Liddle River 1971, Upper Strickland 14 Dec 1979); the 1971 Kuobi forms carry stress apostrophes (sʌ'sa ĩ '1', sʌ'saina '2', di'be '5') — wordlist-only marks, no statement about stress or tone. Notes prefix eyo- when the tally switches sides and dual modifier beyõ. States that only 'Three Febi word lists, recorded in the 1970s, are available in Summer Institute of Linguistics ar…

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project (2010). Fembe Swadesh List [agl]. Internet Archive item rosettaproject_agl_swadesh-1 (4.8 KB).
sources.note: Bare gloss:form list (all: gɔ̃gɔ̃dò / gogonda / ɔ̃gɔ̃dɔ; back: tò-diò..). A few forms carry grave accents with no key or statement — wordlist marks only, not a stress or tone statement.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. (1975). Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1. Pacific Linguistics C-38, pp. 345-460
sources.note: Section 2.6.2.2.6.5.2 'Agala' (p. 392): 'The only material available in this language is a short word list (unpublished) which shows that it is fairly closely related to Nomad.' Only pronouns are given. The phonological note for the family (p. 391) is for Nomad (Samo dialect) alone: nasalisation phonemic, 'There is some evidence that the language has contrastive pitch.' Nothing on Agala stress.

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. (ed.) (1973). The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-26 (whole volume; Appendices pp. 539-592, Appendix D.1 = Agala Swadesh-100 wordlist)
sources.note: Appendix D.1 is a bare Swadesh-100 list for Agala; the appendix introduction (p. 541) gives no transcription conventions and no stress marking is described. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel (1973). A tentative classification of the languages of the Mt Bosavi region. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-26, pp. 187-215
sources.note: Lexicostatistical classification only; Agala listed as 'AGALA (East Strickland); Sinale (Telford, CMML)' with the wordlist credited to B. Telford. Nothing on phonology or stress.
199 lexical items from Shaw 1973 and Shaw 1986 only; no stress marking, no phonology.
Cites only Ethnologue, Shaw 1973/1986 and McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 wordlist data; nothing on stress.
